answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy requires each identity to hold a unique opal-based hardware token that periodically proves presence by reporting the exact gale intensity and direction at a designated oasis sensor array. The private key stays sealed inside the opal and activates only after matching the live weather signature. An attacker creating thousands of fakes must buy, deploy and maintain that many physical tokens at real oasis sites, imposing a linear hardware and logistics cost that scales with headcount instead of being free software copies.
